verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's own docs show native integrations that create Slack channels, Jira tickets and Zoom meetings via Runbooks. Slack also works as a two-way surface: `/fh` commands run inside incident channels, and `/fh update` posts flow back into FireHydrant's status page. Zoom feeds transcription back into the incident. missing for 10: any evidence of Microsoft Teams or GitHub integrations, documented bidirectional state sync for Jira (only ticket creation is shown), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, the platform integrates with the tools around the incident — Jira, Slack, Teams, Zoom, GitHub — so state flows both ways

citations.quote: Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more
Some examples of actions include creating a Slack channel, starting a Zoom meeting
From Slack, inside an incident channel, you can browse the list of triggered Runbooks for this by executing `/fh`.
All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal Status Page
FireHydrant currently supports meeting transcription for our Google Calendar and Zoom integrations.
